title: What is the bill when a third friend joins?
description: A third friend joins and orders the same cutlet and rasgulla. The share, forty three plus twenty four, goes in a bracket with a three in front, and the bracket is opened into three cutlets and three rasgullas. Keeko doubts that the three reaches only the forty three.
teaching_notes: One idea: three equal shares are three times the whole share, so the three multiplies every term in the bracket. Watch for students who multiply only the first number in the bracket.

source: A third friend, {{NAME_4}}, joins and orders the same. Write the
video_script.why: A learner sees the same bracket idea with three friends, and finds the value two ways that agree.
video_script.substitution: Replace three friends with any number of friends and the bracket works the same way.
video_script.anchor: the hotel bill of three friends who each order a vegetable cutlet and a rasgulla, the book's own order
video_script.wrong_answer: the three multiplies only the forty three
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies only the cutlet price by 3, so the rasgullas of the other friends are left out
video_script.payoff_line: Together the three friends pay two hundred and one rupees.

final_answer.spoken: together the three friends pay two hundred and one rupees

names.{{NAME_1}}: one of the first two friends at the hotel
names.{{NAME_3}}: the other of the first two friends at the hotel
names.{{NAME_4}}: the third friend who joins and orders the same

video_script.design: The same bill as before with a third share card added. The bracket gets a three in front, then opens into three cutlets and three rasgullas.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; three share cards, each with a cutlet card marked ₹43 and a rasgulla card marked ₹24

marks.h3: a third share card joins them

narration: <bookmark mark='h1'/>This is a question from your book about a bill at a hotel.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>{{NAME_1}} and {{NAME_3}} each order a cutlet for forty three rupees and a rasgulla for twenty four rupees.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>Then {{NAME_4}} joins them and orders the same.
<bookmark mark='h4'/>How can we write the total for all three friends?

beats.on_screen: the three share cards stay on the board and the question mark keeps glowing

marks.t1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='t1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: three equal share cards, each 43 plus 24, then one bracket round a single share card with a 3 in front

marks.g1: one share card is drawn as 43 + 24
marks.g3: a bracket closes round one share and a 3 moves in front

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Each friend pays one share, which is a cutlet and a rasgulla.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Three friends order the same, so there are three equal shares.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>Three times the whole share needs the share inside a bracket, with the three in front.

beats.on_screen: Given: three friends, each orders a cutlet ₹43 and a rasgulla ₹24

marks.gv1: the number of friends is written

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, three friends order the same food.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>Each orders a cutlet for forty three rupees and a rasgulla for twenty four rupees.

beats.on_screen: To find: the total with a bracket, the bracket removed, and the value

marks.fd1: the three things to find are listed

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to write the total with a bracket, remove the bracket and find the value.
<bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, write the share of one friend as forty three plus twenty four.

marks.s21: the share goes inside a bracket
marks.s22: a 3 appears in front of the bracket

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, put the share in a bracket.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>Three friends pay three equal shares.
The total is three times open bracket forty three plus twenty four close bracket.

marks.s31: the 3 is copied in front of 43 and in front of 24
marks.s33: the second product 3 × 24 is written beside the first

narration: <bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, remove the bracket, because the three multiplies each number inside it.
<bookmark mark='s33'/>That gives three times forty three plus three times twenty four, for three cutlets and three rasgullas.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>This is one hundred and twenty nine plus seventy two.

marks.s41: the bracket is worked out first as 67
marks.s42: 3 × 67 is written beside the opened form

narration: <bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, check by working out the bracket first.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>Forty three plus twenty four is sixty seven, and the total is three times sixty seven.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 129 + 72 = 201 and 3 × 67 = 201, so the total is 201 rupees
narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>Together the three friends pay two hundred and one rupees.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Both ways give the same amount, so the opened bracket is right.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='k1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 3 × 43 + 24; the bubble is struck out and 3 × 43 + 3 × 24 takes its place

marks.k2: Keeko's bubble shows the three beside the forty three only
marks.k3: an arrow shows the 3 reaching the 24 as well

narration: <bookmark mark='k2'/>Keeko thinks the three multiplies only the forty three.
<bookmark mark='k3'/>But then only one rasgulla is paid for, and there are three friends.
<bookmark mark='k4'/>The three multiplies every number inside the bracket.
